summary: Returns the value as a callable value, or throws.
description: The cheap test — `typeof value === "function"` — which is what you want before calling something. `isFunction` is the stricter reading of the same question.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a callable value.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireFunctionLike(function () {}); // => function () {}
requireFunctionLike(Math.max); // => Math.max
requireFunctionLike(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireFunctionLike({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
